text.p: French energy group Total SA said on Wednesday it had a 150-percent increase in 1996 net income to 5.6 billion francs ($1 billion), helped by the absence of special charges and positive external factors.
The profit figure was in line with analysts' expectations.
Total reported a 37-percent increase in operating income to 10.2 billion francs, boosted by a 63-percent increase in income from upstream activities to 7.3 billion francs.
Total said that external factors, a rise in the price of Brent, improved European refining margins and a higher dollar had contributed 2.0 billion to operating income.
Internal growth and productivity efforts added 1.6 billion francs but increased expenses cut 0.3 billion.

Last year, Total took 1.5 billion francs in exceptional charges for the application of new U.S. accounting standards and restructuring charges. In 1996 it took a 500 million franc charge at the operating level for the Lylle-Frigg platform offshore Norway.
Total said it planned to increase capital spending to 18 billion in 1997 from 16 billion in 1996.

Return on equity was 10.3 percent in 1996, in line with a plan to raise it to 10 percent in 1998 and 12 percent in 2000. Total said it expected ongoing productivity efforts would allow a further improvement in profitability in the next few years. ($ = 5.564 French Francs)
